items.headline: Nvidia Shrinks Neocloud Backing to $32 Billion as CoreWeave and Nebius Rallies Fade Fast / Nvidia clarifies when it will - and won't - keep financing neoclouds / Moody's cuts Nvidia outlook to stable, saying Huang's exit clouds strategy and policy
items.claim: Barchart via Yahoo (18 Nov 15:13Z): Nvidia's financing commitments to neoclouds fell to USD 32bn from USD 36bn the prior quarter; they activate only after a provider secures its own financing and brings capacity online, and delayed projects forfeit support; Kress framed future support as 'disciplined and selective'; CRWV -3.5%, IREN -2.4%, NBIS cut a ~4% gain to ~1%. TechCrunch (18 Nov 13:00Z): Kress - 'what we are indicating in our statement there is that is when our guarantee starts'; if a project stalls the guarantee 'doesn't exist anymore'; 'the availability of land, power, shell is such a critical part of the whole structure'; Nvidia is 'taking a very strong look in terms of the types of companies that we would want to help in terms of the financing'; guaranteeing a loan does not mean Nvidia provides the financing; the OpenAI PORTS-Pike (Ohio) backstop was reduced to USD 105bn from USD 250bn; Kress called it a clarification of existing terms not previously disclosed, not a policy change. investinglive (22:36Z): Moody's lowered Nvidia's outlook to stable from positive, 'the resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang is credit negative', citing uncertainty over strategy and financial policies, possible effects on AI partnerships and governance/operational weaknesses including export controls; no near-term upgrade. Newsquawk 19 Nov: Nvidia 'wiped out its post-earnings gains'; Trump says Blackwell sales to China could be permitted in 2-3 years.
items.candidate_dial: C-credit (neocloud backstop tightening - conditional guarantees, smaller commitment) / C-capex
items.source: Barchart via Yahoo 18 Nov 15:13Z; TechCrunch 18 Nov 13:00Z; investinglive 18 Nov 22:36Z; heygotrade 19 Nov; Newsquawk 19 Nov 07:02Z

items.name: Moonshot AI scraps USD 150m deal to rent Nvidia Blackwell (Ultra B300) access through an Indonesian data centre after this week's US remote-access rule; reportedly re-contracts with another SE Asian cloud (The Information via KuCoin/Newsquawk) - pulled compute deal, private Chinese lab, regulatory cause
items.headline: China's Moonshot AI has reportedly scrapped its USD 150mln deal to rent access to NVIDIA's Blackwell Ultra B300 chips through an Indonesian data centre / Moonshot AI Cancels $150 Million Nvidia Chip Rental Deal Amid U.S. Export Restrictions
items.claim: KuCoin (19 Nov 02:55Z, relaying ChainCatcher/The Information, two sources): Moonshot AI cancelled a USD 150m contract to lease Nvidia Blackwell computing power through a data centre in Indonesia after new US regulations 'restricting Chinese companies' remote access to advanced chips' announced this week; it has a replacement Blackwell Ultra B300 contract with a different Southeast Asian cloud provider. Newsquawk (19 Nov): same report, headline only. Context (Yahoo 17 Nov): the Commerce interim final rule adds licence requirements for advanced chips sent to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil and tightens foundry/packager checks, effective on its 19 Nov publication; Newsquawk 19 Nov headlines say TSMC and Samsung suspended certain shipments to Chinese customers (FT) and Samsung Foundry may halt production for some Chinese designers (unverified).
items.candidate_dial: C-capex (pulled compute-rental deal - export-control driven, non-hyperscaler)
items.source: KuCoin flash 19 Nov 02:55Z (The Information via ChainCatcher); Newsquawk 19 Nov; Yahoo/Commerce rule 17 Nov
items.note: Fails the hard-event definition (not a hyperscaler or registered ticker; cause is regulation, not demand or financing) and the lab reportedly replaced the capacity elsewhere. Recorded because it is the only outright cancelled deal dated in gate and because it pairs with the Taiwan sell-off and the 11-16 Malaysia DC-loan syndication delay as SE-Asia compute-channel friction. The Information primary and cryptobriefing (client_error) not read.

items.name: Anthropic IPO Japan tranche below plan: 36.1m Class A shares vs 38.5-50m planned, ~USD 3bn at the low end of the 3-3.5bn target, attributed to Japanese institutions' reduced capacity after Kioxia/SoftBank losses (>40% this quarter) - while the overall IPO priced at USD 83 above the 70-78 range for a record USD 107.3bn (calendar-group context)
items.headline: Anthropic pulls in roughly $3 billion from Japan in IPO slice / Anthropic IPO Raises $3 Billion in Japan, Reaching Lower End of Fundraising Range
items.claim: Briefs (18 Nov, relaying Bloomberg): the Japan tranche sold 36.1m Class A shares at USD 83, below the planned 38.5-50m, raising about USD 3bn at the low end of the expected 3-3.5bn, ~3.7% of the deal; Aizawa Securities' Ikuo Mitsui said pressure on Kioxia and SoftBank Group positions (both down over 40% this quarter) may have 'reduced investors' capacity' to buy; overall Anthropic issued 956.4m shares plus 23.6m founder shares for USD 107.3bn including a private placement. Newsquawk (19 Nov): regulatory filing confirms 36.1m shares at USD 83, below the planned 38.5-50m and the USD 3-3.5bn target. Reuters via Yahoo: priced at USD 83 above range, raised USD 81bn in the IPO proper, ~USD 1.5tn fully diluted, first trade Thursday. Eiseman: gray market +20-26%, retail allocation expected below 20%, institutional demand several times the offer.
items.candidate_dial: C-equity (issuance absorption - a downsized regional tranche inside an upsized record IPO)
items.source: Briefs 18 Nov (Bloomberg); Newsquawk 19 Nov; Reuters via Yahoo 19 Nov; Eiseman ICYMI 19 Nov
items.note: The IPO itself belongs to the calendar group; this item records only the one piece that reads as an events category - a tranche sized below plan with a stated capacity reason (Japanese tech losses). It does NOT meet the hard-event definition: the deal as a whole was upsized and priced above range. First-day trading outcome after run time.
